answer: Every claimant dives for pearls in a glacier-fed bay. The registry hands each claim one plot, and the claimant sweeps it in a spiral around the marker, collects five oysters, and opens them before a witness, who weighs any pearl found and records it before the epoch closes. One dive costs a $180 boat, $60 of gear, and a $40 licence, so a farm of 100 fakes pays $28,000 for boats, gear, and licences — and a pearl found on one plot can only ever count for the claim that was assigned it.
